alertDetailsOverride.alertDisplayNameFormat: New account {{NewUser}} granted a role within an hour of creation
alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: Account {{NewUser}} was created at {{CreatedTime}} and granted a directory role by {{Actor}} within the following hour.

properties.query:
let NewAccounts = AuditLogs
    | where OperationName =~ "Add user" and Result =~ "success"
    | mv-expand TargetResources
    | extend NewUser = tostring(TargetResources.userPrincipalName)
    | where isnotempty(NewUser)
    | project NewUser, CreatedTime = TimeGenerated;
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where OperationName =~ "Add member to role" and Result =~ "success"
| mv-expand TargetResources
| extend NewUser = tostring(TargetResources.userPrincipalName)
| where isnotempty(NewUser)
| extend Actor = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)
| join kind=inner (NewAccounts) on NewUser
| where TimeGenerated > CreatedTime
| where datetime_diff("minute", TimeGenerated, CreatedTime) <= 60
| project TimeGenerated, Actor, NewUser, CreatedTime, OperationName, CorrelationId
| extend Account = NewUser
properties.displayName: Entra - New Account Granted Role Within One Hour
properties.description:
DETECTS
An account created and then assigned a directory role within sixty minutes, correlating two AuditLogs event types.

WHY IT MATTERS
This sequence is the classic attacker persistence pattern: create an innocuous account, elevate it, then use it as a durable backdoor that survives remediation of the originally compromised identity. Legitimate provisioning almost always separates account creation from role assignment by an approval step, so the compressed timeline is itself the signal (MITRE T1136, Create Account).

TRIAGE
1. Identify the new account naming. Attackers often mimic service accounts or existing user patterns.
2. Determine what role was granted and by whom.
3. Confirm whether an onboarding request exists for this person.
4. Check whether the new account has signed in, and from where.
5. If unauthorized: disable the account immediately, then investigate the creating identity as compromised.

FALSE POSITIVES
Automated provisioning pipelines that create and entitle accounts in one workflow, and admin-created service accounts. Tune by excluding the provisioning service principal.

SOURCE
AuditLogs

TUNING HISTORY (2026-08-02)
The role-grant side of the query is now anchored to the current evaluation window with
where TimeGenerated > ago(1h), matching queryFrequency. Without that anchor the rule
re-discovered the same historical AuditLogs pair on every hourly run for as long as it
remained inside the 1-day queryPeriod, producing 24 alerts per account for one real event
- 48 alerts for the two break-glass accounts, still firing 23 hours later. The NewAccounts
subquery deliberately keeps the full queryPeriod lookback so an account created up to a day
earlier is still correlated; only the trigger side is windowed. Incident grouping is now
keyed on Account over a 1-day lookback.
